scope: Independent primary-source spot check, 9 of the chapter's 10 references. Custom Catalog, pin/GC and cutover contracts remain explicit chapter design requirements.

sources.method: web access failed; fetched exact primary PDF with urllib and inspected pdftotext output
sources.supports: T1 has 85 billion records and 87 TB raw. The one-field MR/Dremel comparison reads about 0.5TB compressed versus 87TB record-oriented data. No transferable latency claim.
Column layout alone is insufficient: compression, late materialization and block/vector execution contribute. The chapter correctly labels 3/20 and 4:1 as assumptions.
Metadata locates selected column chunks within row groups; predicate columns remain required input.
Old/new layouts coexist; metadata evolution does not eagerly rewrite files. Version 1.10.0 is explicit, not called latest.
Atomic metadata-pointer exchange, refresh after conflict and operation-specific assumptions before retry. The chapter does not attribute custom accepted(table,batch) atomicity to Iceberg.

sources.location: Sequence Numbers / Row-level Deletes / Scan Planning, v2-scoped claims
sources.supports: V2 delete files and sequence applicability are needed for live rows. Newer v3/v4 features are outside the illustrated v2 contract.

sources.location: Remove orphan files / Compact data files
sources.supports: Short orphan-retention windows can delete in-progress files; compaction reduces file-open/metadata work. The chapter's explicit pin/fence protocol is a requirement, not a claimed built-in API.

sources.location: An alternative, replay steps and per-partition offset background
sources.supports: Replay a new processor into another output table and switch after catch-up. The chapter explicitly defines its own next-offset half-open convention and recoverable continuation barrier.
Strong object read-after-write and atomic single-key updates do not provide atomic cross-key publication. No live object-store behavior was tested.
